top_news.title: India forces caller-ID apps to feed spam reports to telcos
top_news.dek: India's telecom regulator now requires caller-ID apps to share user-reported spam data with telecom operators via a blockchain platform.
top_news.brief: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has mandated that apps allowing users to flag spam must feed that data into a centralized blockchain system managed by telcos. Truecaller and other providers argue this requirement is anti-competitive, as it forces them to hand over proprietary, commercially valuable datasets to the very telecom operators they often compete with.
top_news.image_alt: TRAI regulatory logo and smartphone interface

top_news.title: Cache-to-Cache: Direct Semantic Communication Between LLMs (2025)
top_news.dek: A new research paper proposes 'Cache-to-Cache' communication, allowing LLMs to exchange internal representations directly to bypass text-based latency.
top_news.brief: Current multi-LLM systems rely on text-based communication, which introduces tokenization overhead and loses semantic depth. The proposed method enables direct transfer of KV-Cache semantics between models, potentially improving response quality and reducing generation latency by avoiding the need to convert internal states into output tokens.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing direct KV-Cache transfer between two LLM architectures

top_news.title: [AINews] Here are 6 Clones of Jev in 2 days
top_news.dek: The 'Jev' model architecture has triggered a wave of rapid cloning, with six implementations appearing within 48 hours of its launch.
top_news.brief: Following the high-profile release of the 'Jev' system-one model, the developer community has produced six functional clones in just two days. The original launch video garnered 36 million views, signaling significant interest in the model's specific approach to system-one reasoning and decision-making.
top_news.image_alt: X social media interface showing viral AI model discussion

top_news.title: Introducing the Australian Youth Safety Blueprint
top_news.dek: OpenAI has released a six-pillar 'Australian Youth Safety Blueprint' aimed at establishing standards for AI usage among minors.
top_news.brief: The framework outlines guidelines for AI literacy, age-appropriate safeguards, and privacy-focused age verification. It serves as a policy proposal for the Australian market, emphasizing parental controls and crisis support integration to ensure that AI tools remain safe and constructive for younger users.
top_news.image_alt: Document cover for the Australian Youth Safety Blueprint

top_news.title: convaiinnovations/laya (0 downloads, 209 likes)
top_news.dek: Laya is a non-autoregressive, multilingual decision model designed for high-speed, typed output without text generation.
top_news.brief: Laya processes inputs like emails or JSON and returns typed answers with calibrated probabilities in a single 33ms forward pass. By using Reinforcement Learning with Calibrated Decisions (RLCD), it avoids hallucination and text generation entirely, focusing instead on providing reliable, structured data across over 100 languages.
top_news.image_alt: Performance comparison chart between Laya and Jev models
